observable_outcome: An error the request did not cause no longer leaves the API as the caller's mistake, on any route. Measured at 9a09ef8, internal/api/api.go:1116 domainError sets status 400 and code invalid_request as its default (api.go:1127-1128), overrides that for eight sentinel groups, and then answers with err.Error() as the response message (api.go:1168); all 24 call sites -- 19 handlers in api.go, five in repositories.go, and the /internal/reconcile branch at api.go:94 -- inherit it. That is why a storage-side gRPC InvalidArgument reached the caller as a bad request, with the Firestore parent name in the body, and why a broken cursor read as a refused cursor for three exercises. The repair is the default itself: 500 internal_error with a fixed message, the same triple the panic-recovery branch already answers (api.go:49-53), plus one positive branch errors.Is(err, application.ErrInvalidRequest) and an explicit list of the existing exported caller-fault sentinels. Classification is by sentinel identity only, never by a dependency's text. What makes it safe is a route pin table written and measured GREEN ON THE UNEDITED TREE first, so that every status code that existed before still exists after; V2-079's cursor refusals stay 400 and its two accepted shapes stay 200 with its test byte-unchanged; an injected store fault is asserted, on every route and in both the fault-instead-of-callback and fault-after-callback shapes, to answer 500 and never 400 and never a 2xx, with none of the injected text in the body.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, written into both evidence records BEFORE any source file is edited, as a table with one row each. (1) What this task makes true: an error the request did not cause leaves the API as 500 internal_error rather than 400 invalid_request, on every one of the 24 domainError call sites, and it carries no dependency text. (2) What it deliberately does not do: it moves no existing status code and no existing response message (A3 and A6 measure it), it edits internal/domain not at all, it edits no contract document, it adds no logging, it adds no route and no field, and it changes no error's Error() text. (3) What it records but does not fix: that contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml declares neither '500' nor '400' for four routes that call domainError (dp-v2-083 d11a), that this repository has no logging idiom at all so the dependency's own text is now visible nowhere in-process (d11b), and that domain.ErrInvalidTransition and application.ErrDuplicateRequest stay 400 though a state-machine refusal arguably deserves 409 (d9). (4) What only a later task can establish: nothing -- this task's outcome is fully assertable here, and A8 is executed rather than skipped. (5) That this task passes no release gate on its own.

A2. Baseline, measured before changing anything. EVERY line number and EVERY count in this Work Order was read by the coordinator at 9a09ef8 and is expected to be stale: the last nine tasks each found at least one disagreement. Re-measure each with devbox run --pure -- go test -list '.*' ./<pkg> and a fresh grep, use the measured value, and report every disagreement in the evidence rather than the value written here. Top-level test counts read by grep at 9a09ef8: internal/api 54, internal/application 180, internal/domain 54, internal/contracts 33. Record before and after counts per touched package; the after count must be the before count plus exactly the tests A3, A6, A7 and A9 add, and no existing test may be deleted or renamed.

A3. THE PIN TABLE, and it is written FIRST. Add one table-driven test to internal/api/api_test.go -- TestEveryRouteStillAnswersTheStatusItAnsweredBefore -- with one row per (method, path, role, body) case, covering every route the router reaches: /healthz, /internal/reconcile, the three /v1/runner/enrollment paths, /owner and /owner/assets/, GET and POST /v1/requirements, GET /v1/requirements/{id}, both needs-input verbs, GET and POST /v1/controls, GET /v1/queue/summary, GET /v1/runners, GET /v1/providers, GET /v1/export, GET /v1/release/state, POST /v1/runner/claims:acquire, POST /v1/runner/permits:check, POST /v1/executions/result, POST /v1/executions/{id}:start, POST /v1/leases/{id}:renew, POST /v1/runner/heartbeat, POST /v1/runner/checkpoints, and the five /v1/repositories cases including :retire and :observe. Each row asserts the status AND the error code. Cover, per route, at least: the success case, the unauthenticated case, the wrong-role case, a malformed-body case, and every refusal the route can produce today. Run this test GREEN ON THE UNEDITED TREE, and record the entire measured table -- every row with its measured status and code -- in the api evidence record as the baseline, with the argv that produced it. Only then proceed to A4. A table written after the flip proves nothing.

A4. The default. In internal/api/api.go's domainError, replace the two default assignments (status := http.StatusBadRequest and code := "invalid_request", api.go:1127-1128 at 9a09ef8) with an unclassified default of http.StatusInternalServerError and code internal_error, and make the final call answer with a CONSTANT message -- byte-identical to the panic-recovery branch's "internal server error" (api.go:49-53) -- instead of err.Error(). The eight already-classified branches keep err.Error() so that no existing response message changes. Add exactly one new positive branch, errors.Is(err, application.ErrInvalidRequest) -> 400 invalid_request, and one explicitly commented list of the already-exported sentinels that are caller faults and are not among the eight -- at minimum application.ErrInvalidCursor, and every other one A3's table proves reachable as a 400. Name internal/domain's sentinels from here if needed; internal/domain is prohibited and must be byte-unchanged. Do not classify by any error's text, by a type assertion on an adapter type, or by a gRPC status code.

A5. The caller-fault marker, message-transparent. Add internal/application/errors.go holding the exported sentinel ErrInvalidRequest plus an unexported constructor that marks an authored validation error so errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRequest) is true while Error() returns the ORIGINAL text unchanged (Error() delegates, Unwrap() returns the wrapped error, Is(target) matches ErrInvalidRequest). Do NOT spell it as fmt.Errorf("%w: ...", ErrInvalidRequest) anywhere: that prepends the sentinel's text to the response message and is a body change this task forbids itself. Apply the marker ONLY at sites that author a caller-input validation error and that A3's table proves reachable as a 400 -- known candidates measured at 9a09ef8: internal/application/service.go:24-29 requireRequest, internal/application/readmodels.go:126, :358 and :450. Apply it at the AUTHORING site, never at a shared helper, never in Service.transact or Service.mutate, and never around a transaction. If a wrap appears necessary in an internal/application file this Work Order does not list, stop and escalate rather than adding the file.

A6. Nothing moved, and it is measured rather than promised. Re-run A3's pin table after A4 and A5 and record the after table next to the before table in the evidence, row by row. Every row's status and code must be identical. Then run devbox run --pure -- go test ./... and devbox run --pure -- go vet ./...: internal/application, internal/reconciler and internal/runner assert error identities that a wrap must not disturb. If any pin-table row moves, or any package outside the touched two goes red, the design was departed from: stop and escalate to the tech_lead. Do not adjust a row, do not weaken an assertion, and do not add a route-specific case in internal/api to hold a row in place.

A7. The repair, asserted per route and in both fault shapes. Add TestAStorageFaultIsNotReportedAsTheCallersMistake to internal/api/api_test.go: a test-local decorator over the application.Transactor port, in two variants -- (A) it returns the fault INSTEAD of running the callback, (B) it runs the callback to completion and THEN returns the fault, which is the commit-time shape -- driven against every route that reaches domainError. For each route and each variant assert: status 500; code internal_error; the status is NOT 400 and NOT any 2xx (non_goals item 2); the body contains no part of the injected error's text (non_goals item 3); the body carries exactly the four keys error, message, schema_version and correlation_id; and the X-Correlation-ID header is still set. Inject a plain errors.New carrying storage-shaped text -- a doubled Firestore parent name with a byte offset, copied from V2-079's measurement -- and do NOT import a gRPC status package: internal/ci derives the manifest from imports and a new edge turns make check red for a reason unrelated to this repair.

A8. V2-079's boundary, unweakened and unedited. TestTheBacklogStillRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue must keep its name, keep every assertion, remain BYTE-UNCHANGED, and pass. Re-measure and record its shape: at 9a09ef8 it pins FIVE refused cursor shapes at 400 invalid_request (fabricated-not-base64url, envelope-version-is-not-v1, truncated-prefix-of-a-real-cursor, another-collections-document-key-space, another-paged-reads-cursor-shape) and TWO accepted shapes at 200 (a v1 envelope naming a Requirement that does not exist, and one naming another aggregate's id). The coordinator's brief said four refused shapes; use the tree's measured count and report the disagreement. If that test needs ANY edit to pass, a caller fault stopped being classified as one: stop and escalate.

A9. The application layer's half, positive and negative. Add to internal/application/errors_test.go a table asserting that every validation refusal reachable from a route satisfies errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRequest) -- capture with no request_id, page_size below 1 and above application.MaxPageSize, an export limit out of range, and every other site A5 marked -- AND, as the negative half, that a fault the request did not cause does NOT satisfy it: a zero-value clock (internal/application/service.go:779, allocation.go:564, runner_version.go:297 and :321, provider_registry.go:742 at 9a09ef8) and a store decorator's storage error. The negative half is not optional: without it the marker drifts toward being applied everywhere, which recreates the defect with a new spelling.

A10. The intended class changes, enumerated and shown unreachable by any request. Record, as a check with its measurement, that each of these becomes 500 and that none of them is reachable through any pin-table row: adapter and gRPC faults surfacing through the port, internal/store/firestore's ErrInvalidSchema and ErrWriteCap and its own "invalid requirement page limit" (internal/store/firestore/store.go:645), "clock returned zero time" at each measured site, context cancellation and deadline expiry, and a failure of the /internal/reconcile hook (internal/api/api.go:93, a 400 today for a reconciliation no caller performed). State in the evidence that domain.ErrInvalidTransition and application.ErrDuplicateRequest deliberately stay 400.

A11. Real persistence, executed rather than reasoned about. Run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive against the real cmd/control-plane binary and the real Firestore emulator: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api. internal/api/live_local_test.go is PROHIBITED -- run it, do not edit it -- and its Backlog cursor walk plus its quota-exhaustion probe are the emulator-backed regression proof that this change moved nothing over real persistence. Record the argv and the verdict line. A bare go test with no emulator is green while measuring nothing; a skipped case is never a pass (gate rule G7). If the emulator cannot be started, record the skips, set the api record to partial and STOP -- do not report a pass. Note that devbox run --pure strips environment variables, so AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL must be passed with -e and never as a shell prefix.

A12. The contract gap, recorded and not touched. contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is prohibited and must be byte-unchanged. Record the measurement: four routes that call domainError declare neither '500' nor '400' -- GET /v1/requirements/{requirement_id} (openapi-v1.yaml:54 at 9a09ef8), GET /v1/controls (:59), GET /v1/queue/summary (:69), GET /v1/export (:127) -- while every other route already declares '500'; nothing enforces response codes, because internal/contracts/release_contract_test.go's openAPIDeclaredPaths (:324-332) extracts path keys only; and the 500 was already reachable on those four routes before this task through the panic-recovery branch, so the gap predates it. Record it as a coordinator-owned follow-up. Editing that document would move the contracts component key and the release BundleDigest and would enrol this task in V2-082's contract chain.

A13. No logging, and the cost stated plainly. Record the measurement that NO non-test file under internal/ or cmd/ imports "log" or "log/slog", so this repository has no logging idiom, and that after A4 the dependency's own text is visible nowhere in-process. State that the correlation id is still returned in the body and in the X-Correlation-ID header and that the fault stays reproducible against the emulator. Do not add a logger, do not add a new response field, and do not put the storage text in a header: any of those violates non_goals item 3. Name the follow-up rather than performing it.

A14. Rollback, recorded as a property. State that rollback is a revert of internal/api/api.go plus internal/application/errors.go and the marked sites, that nothing else must be undone, and why: this change writes no document, reads no document, alters no stored field, adds no route, changes no request or response schema, and changes no error's Error() text, so no data and no client state exists that only the new code can interpret. Verify the message-neutrality claim by measurement rather than assertion: for at least three pin-table 400 rows, the response body is byte-identical before and after.

A15. Evidence. Create .agents/v2/evidence/V2-083-api.json (id ev-v2-083-api, component api) and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-083-application.json (id ev-v2-083-application, component application), each with task_id V2-083 -- the PRODUCING task, never a consuming one -- and correlation_id v2-083-error-classification. Every acceptance item must be traceable to a named check recording the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout and a summary stating the measured result. Record the execution environment for every run: uname -srm, go version as resolved inside devbox run --pure, and the devbox environment. A skipped check is recorded with status skipped and is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Register both with appended entries in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of each artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry and create no third record. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with the records in place. Any digest written in prose is 64 or 40 hex characters followed by at most one punctuation character, and never two revisions joined by a two-dot range. After committing the evidence run devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml; never gitleaks dir .

A16. Evidence keys, for the issued records only. The evidence_key in each record is that component's key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree with every touched file already git-added, because a file not yet in the index is invisible to the git ls-files based input set the key derives from. Measure and record exactly TWO keys: api and application. Under gate rule G6a these checks are re-run by make check, so per-component key equality is a record of provenance and NOT a pass/fail condition: do not measure all 23 component keys, do not copy a key from any earlier record, and do not treat key movement or key stability as a verdict.

A17. Chain position and manifest, recorded as facts for the coordinator. Record that internal/domain/**, contracts/**, internal/store/** and internal/web/** are prohibited BY DESIGN and not by omission (dp-v2-083 d4, d10, d11). Record that this change creates and removes no import edge: internal/api gains no import because it already imports internal/application and internal/domain, and internal/application/errors.go imports only errors and fmt. Because no edge moves, a red manifest or dependency-coverage check means the design was departed from: stop and escalate and do not edit ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. Record that this task must be serialized AFTER V2-082 (which holds internal/api/api.go and internal/api/api_test.go) and BEFORE V2-087 (which holds internal/api/api_test.go), and that V2-080 depends on both.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

Write the pin table FIRST and measure it green on the UNEDITED tree, then flip the default. A table written or adjusted after the flip proves nothing, and adjusting a row to match a new answer turns this task into 'move whatever moved': stop and escalate instead.

Do not classify an error by matching the text a dependency happened to produce, by asserting on an adapter's concrete type, or by reading a gRPC status code. errors.Is against a sentinel is the only material. A9's negative half and A7's absence-of-text assertion are the guards; matching text in a test to prove text is GONE is not classification and is required.

Do not let an unclassified error become a success. A7 variant B -- the fault returned after the callback ran -- is mandatory on every route, and any 2xx there is a failure of this task, not a flaky test.
Do not put a storage message into a response. The new default answers with a constant; err.Error() stays only on the eight already-classified branches. No new response field, no header, no logger.

Do not weaken V2-079's boundary. TestTheBacklogStillRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue stays byte-unchanged and passing: five refused cursor shapes still 400 invalid_request, two accepted shapes still 200. If it needs an edit, stop and escalate.

Do not move any existing status code or any existing response message. If the only way to keep a row green is a route-specific special case in internal/api, the design was departed from: stop and escalate.
Do not edit internal/domain, internal/store, internal/quota, contracts/**, internal/web/** or cmd/**. internal/domain's sentinels are named from internal/api, which already imports the package.

Do not apply the caller-fault marker at a shared helper, in Service.transact or Service.mutate, or around a transaction. It goes at the site that authors the validation error. If a marker is needed in an internal/application file this Work Order does not list, stop and escalate rather than adding the file.

Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. This design creates no new import edge, so a red manifest or dependency-coverage check means the design was departed from: stop and escalate to the tech_lead.

Do not edit .agents/v2/task-state/**, any .agents/v2/packets/** file, any other task's evidence record, any entry in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json belonging to another task, or anything under .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/**.

Start the Firestore emulator for real for A11. A bare go test with no emulator is GREEN while measuring nothing, and a skipped test is never a pass (gate rule G7). If the emulator cannot be started, record the skips, set the api record to partial and STOP -- do not report a pass.

Do not run any Provider CLI. No invocation of claude, codex or opencode is authorised by this task, not even --version or --help, and no live provider evidence record may be issued. TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood is not executed here and internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go is prohibited.
Do not delete or rename any existing test. Every pre-existing top-level test keeps its name and keeps passing.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new or modified test. Clocks are injected, every wait is a bounded deadline poll reusing an existing idiom in the package, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.

Do not run the full devbox run --pure -- make check. go test ./..., go vet ./... and make component-api / make component-application are the implementer's verification; the coordinator runs make check once at integration. Run devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml after the evidence commit; never gitleaks dir .

Judge every devbox run by its verdict line, never by the shell exit status: devbox run's exit code is not reliable in this repository. devbox run --pure also strips environment variables, so AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL must be passed with -e and never as a shell prefix.

Under gate rule G6a, per-component evidence key equality is not a pass/fail condition. Measure exactly the two keys for the records this task issues (api, application); do not measure all 23 and do not treat key movement as a verdict.

Do not cite any capability id in these evidence records, do not edit contracts/release-contract/** and do not edit .agents/v2/evidence/V2-022-release-live-dogfood.json. The capability-evidence reverse check is scoped to V2-022's records and must stay green.

Do not write a module-path string literal into any source or test file: internal/ci's manifest check reads such a literal as an undeclared edge and turns make check red. Build any needed path by concatenating a prefix with a suffix, and confirm every new file after git add.

Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If any acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating, weakening or reinterpreting it.

Every line number and every test count in this Work Order was read at 9a09ef8 and is expected to be stale -- the last nine tasks each found a disagreement, and the coordinator's own brief disagreed with the tree about the number of refused cursor shapes. Re-measure each one yourself with go test -list and a fresh grep, use the measured value, and report every disagreement in the evidence.
